hero.title: Giving robusta a reason to be chosen
hero.intro: Robarica is a Wellington brand selling Vietnamese robusta coffee, grown in the Central Highlands of Vietnam and sold mainly on Amazon in the US. Working with the founder, I redesigned the label of its whole bean pouch, updated its Amazon listing images, adapted the label for a new instant coffee and designed the cover of its brewing guide.

image.alt: The Robarica Coffee of Vietnam pouch lying on a white desk next to a cup of black coffee

p: Robarica sells 100% Vietnamese robusta: dark roasted, low in acidity and naturally high in caffeine. Most people know robusta, if they know it at all, as the cheap filler in instant coffee, and that reputation was the main thing standing between the product and a new customer.

Robarica already had a pouch for its ground coffee, built around the brand's botanical artwork and a serif title. The coffee was changing to 100% robusta whole beans, and the founder wanted a new label that would [[stand out on an Amazon search page]], where most of its customers find it.

blocks.text: The packaging needed to treat robusta as a coffee worth choosing, not a cheaper substitute.

bleed.alt: The Robarica pouch on a wooden table with coffee beans, leaves and a Vietnamese phin filter

sections.heading: Read at the size of a thumbnail

p: On Amazon, most people first see the pouch as a small image in a list of search results, next to a dozen other coffees. The founder's concern was that the old label was hard to read at that size, and that [[the words people actually look for were lost]].

blocks.title: Keywords first, the brand second
p: The founder asked for the label to lead with the words that catch a shopper's attention rather than the brand name: Coffee of Vietnam, Whole Beans and 100% Pure.

I made the logo smaller and rebuilt the text in the black panel in a clear order, with the origin set largest in a wide typeface, then the product, then the roast and purity, and [[espresso and filter in a box of their own]]. The botanical border is the brand's own artwork, so it stayed as the frame.

image.alt: The text from the black panel of the whole bean pouch: Coffee of Viet Nam, Whole Beans, Dark Roast, 100% Pure, and Espresso in a box above Filter
image.caption: The new order in the black panel: origin first, then the product, the roast and purity, and how to brew it.

blocks.title: Tested before it was printed
p: Rather than choosing a label by eye, the founder wanted to test it on the listing. I supplied three main images on white: the old label with coffee beans scattered around it, the new label without beans, and the new label with beans.
He ran them on Amazon, and [[the new label won the test]], so that is the version that went to print.

image.alt: Two Robarica pouches side by side: the original ground coffee label with a serif Coffee of Vietnam title, and the new whole bean label
image.caption: The original ground coffee label and the new whole bean label, as main images on white.

blocks.title: A back label for a new product
p: The back label changed at the same time. The coffee was now 100% robusta rather than a robusta and arabica blend, so the founder rewrote the description, the ingredients and the tasting notes, and the tagline became Steal a heart away.
I set the new copy and added [[a QR code with a Scan me prompt]] that leads to the free brewing guide, so the help is on the pack itself.

image.alt: The brewing steps from the back of the pouch: seven steps for a Vietnamese phin filter and seven for an espresso machine, each with an icon
image.caption: The brewing steps on the back label, for a phin filter and an espresso machine.

blocks.title: The same label, a new product
p: Later, the label was adapted for a new instant 3-in-1 coffee. The front keeps the same frame, logo and order, with [[only the product name changing]], so the two products sit together as one family.
The back follows the same layout but carries what instant coffee needs instead: a one-minute method, the ingredients and quality details, and the same QR code to the brewing guide.

sections.heading: The first look is a product page

p: Robarica sells mainly on Amazon, so for many people the listing images are their first proper look at the coffee. All six had been made for the earlier ground coffee, so they needed updating to match the new pouch and the new product.

I put the main image on a pure white background, updated the zip at the top and made the pack brighter so it reads well on screen. I added the new label to the packaging image, made [[100% pure and 100% Vietnamese]] easier to read, and corrected the copy on the others so every claim matched 100% robusta, from the tasting notes to how the beans are roasted.

p: Robusta can be unforgiving when it is brewed casually, and a harsh first cup can easily turn into a bad review. The ebook, How to Make a Perfect Cup of Coffee, is a practical brewing guide: part education, part product support, and part confidence for first-time customers.

The founder's brief for the cover was specific. It needed the Robarica look and feel without the logo or the brand name, a title that [[stands out among the other coffee books on Amazon]], and a familiar cup of coffee rather than a Vietnamese phin, because most of the audience is in the US.

The inside is mostly text, so the cover does most of the work. The author chose the final design from eight drafts, and I supplied it as a Kindle cover, a PDF book cover, 3D images for Facebook ads and a paperback cover. The ebook is

blocks.text: A harsh first cup can easily become a bad review, so the guide reaches people before they brew.
